standard.title: Present with responsible media practice
standard.description: present media arts works in informal and/or formal settings using responsible media practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share media arts works in informal settings applying permission and credits. They have not yet presented in formal settings, used internet-based platforms for distribution, or reflected systematically on how different audiences receive the same work.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present media arts works in informal and/or formal settings using responsible media practice, considering how audiences and platforms shape reception.

nodes.label: Responsible media practice for formal and digital settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply responsible media practices appropriate to formal or digital presentation contexts — including legal, ethical and cultural considerations.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two responsible media practice requirements for a formal or digital sharing context (e.g. online safety, cultural protocols, copyright) and apply them when preparing to present.
nodes.typical_width: Apply responsible media practices across informal and formal contexts and digital platforms — legal, ethical and moral considerations; online safety protocols; cultural protocols for representing community or cultural stories; copyright and attribution; engaging appropriately with audience responses online.
wider: Investigate protocols for representing community or cultural stories in media arts works before creating and presenting a work — documenting the protocol decisions made and reflecting on how cultural understandings shaped the final presentation choices

Research responsible media practice requirements for sharing on a specific digital platform (school LMS, community website) — developing a checklist that addresses legal, ethical and cultural considerations specific to that platform
nodes.hinge_reason: Responsible media practice for digital and formal settings requires explicit application — without it, online sharing creates legal, ethical and cultural compliance gaps that cannot be remedied after the fact.

response_modes.reason: Use scenario-based reasoning to build transferable responsible media practice: 'Before we upload this to the school website, what do we need to check? Why does each check matter?' Apply to real planned sharing activities.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two responsible media practice requirements for their planned presentation context
Student applies both requirements when presenting and can explain why each is needed in this context

nodes.label: Presenting across settings and audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present a media arts work to audiences in more than one setting — reflecting on how and why the work may be received differently across settings.
nodes.minimum_width: Present a media arts work to at least one audience and reflect on at least one way the setting or audience affected how the work was received.
nodes.typical_width: Present media arts works in informal and formal settings (classroom, school assembly, online platform); reflect on differences in reception across settings; engage with audience responses on digital platforms applying online safety; consider how understandings of culture shape audience experience.
wider: Present a short film to multiple audiences in different settings (classroom, school assembly, digital platform) — reflecting systematically on how and why the work was received differently in each context, and what this reveals about the relationship between audience, setting and meaning

Present a media arts work using internet-based technologies on a curated digital platform (school LMS) — applying online safety and responsible media practice, engaging with audience responses thoughtfully, and reflecting on how the online audience differs from a live audience

response_modes.reason: Presenting across settings integrates production, responsible media practice and audience awareness — support students in treating reception differences as information about communication, not just approval ratings.

Vary the presentation settings — informal classroom, formal assembly, digital platform, community context — so students develop genuine experience of how setting and audience shape reception across multiple contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of presentation settings at Y5-6 (informal classroom, formal assembly, digital platform, community context) and the reflective comparison across them is genuinely rich for developing audience awareness.
success_criteria: Student presents a media arts work to at least one audience applying relevant responsible media practices
Student can reflect on at least one aspect of how the audience or setting shaped the reception of the work
